subject: RFP: Third-Party Roster + EU Cloud change — evidence and fallthrough plan
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@bigenterprise.com>
To: security@redwoodinference.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Cc: security-rfp@bigenterprise.com
Date: 2027-05-04T08:12:00Z
Subject: RFP request — updated third-party roster + planned cloud change for EU region

Hi Redwood team,

Thanks for the quick intro call earlier. As part of our procurement/security review for BigEnterprise's AI platform RFP (RFP-8732) we need an updated third-party roster plus details about a planned cloud change you mentioned on that call. Specifically:

- A machine-readable roster of subprocessors/vendor names, roles (storage, CDN, monitoring, logging), and country of operation.
- Confirmation whether any customer data (logs, metrics, S3-equivalents) will move from GCP to Azure in the EU region or to any new cloud providers. If a change is planned, we need your change-notice window, rollback strategy, and fallback (cross-region) plan.
- Copies of your latest SOC 2 / equivalent attestation and any KMS/HSM provider mappings for EU keys.

Can you send those materials and a point-of-contact for follow-ups by EOD Wednesday? Also please include any links to diagrams or evidence in Drive or shared storage.

Best,
Alice Monroe
Senior Security Sourcing Manager
BigEnterprise Inc.

--
Attachment: rfp_request_8732.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@bigenterprise.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, security-rfp@bigenterprise.com
Date: 2027-05-04T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP request — updated third-party roster + planned cloud change for EU region

Alice — thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick summary and what we'll deliver by EOD Wednesday: 

1) Third-party roster (CSV) with role and country — attached as third_party_roster_20270504.csv.
2) Change notice summary for the EU cloud swap (GCP -> Azure option) including notification window, rollback, and test plan — attached as change_notice_summary_stephanie_20270504.txt.
3) SOC2 attestation (most recent) — attached SOC2_Attestation_2026.pdf.
4) Network/dataflow diagram and KMS mapping will follow in a separate email from Ben with the technical appendix (we expect to include firewall rules, VPC peering notes, and key custody details).

Short answers to your bullets:
- Planned change: we are piloting an additional EU-hosted region on Azure to improve multi-cloud resilience. No customer data will be moved without your approval; the pilot will target non-production telemetry first.
- Notification window: standard 30-day advance notice for production-facing moves, 14 days for non-prod pilot.
- Rollback: fully scripted rollback with immutable snapshots and cross-region replication; estimated RTO < 2 hours for config re-pointing and < 6 hours for data restoration in the unlikely event of failure.

Point of contact: Ben Carter (ben_carter@redwoodinference.com) — he will share the ops diagrams and the KMS/HSM mapping. Laura Bennett in Legal is cc'd for contract/notice language.

Thanks — we'll follow up with the technical appendix within 24 hours.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: third_party_roster_20270504.csv, change_notice_summary_stephanie_20270504.txt, SOC2_Attestation_2026.pdf

From: security-rfp@bigenterprise.com
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@bigenterprise.com>
Date: 2027-05-05T09:30:00Z
Subject: Clarification — telemetry vs. customer PII, and subprocessor notification SLA

Hi Stephanie / Ben,

A couple of quick clarifications so we can score the RFP correctly: 

- When you say "non-production telemetry" for the pilot, can you confirm that it will not include any customer PII or identifiable records?
- For the 30-day notice for production moves, is that a contractual obligation (i.e., will it be written into the DPA/contract), or a standard practice you plan to follow?
- If Azure becomes an active region, will logs/metrics be stored in a different subprocessor (e.g., a third-party ELK host) that operates outside the EU?

If you can answer these three bullets concisely we can proceed to the security scoring phase.

Thanks,
BigEnterprise Security RFP Desk

--
Attachment: scoring_template.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: security-rfp@bigenterprise.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@bigenterprise.com>, laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-05T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Clarification — telemetry vs. customer PII, and subprocessor notification SLA

Thanks for the questions — short answers and then detail below.

Short answers:
- Telemetry pilot: no customer PII will be included. Pilot uses synthetic or de-identified traces; we can provide sample scrub rules.
- Notice window: 30-day notice for production changes will be included in the DPA as a contractual notice clause (we'll propose language).
- Logs/metrics: currently logs are ingested into our ELK-managed cluster run by FastEdge (cdnops@fastedge.net) operating in the EU. We do not plan to move log ownership outside the EU as part of this pilot.

Details:
- Data residency: customer request/production data remains in the customer-selected region. The Azure pilot replicates non-prod telemetry to an Azure EU West tenant under our control; production data movement requires explicit customer opt-in/contract amendment.
- KMS/HSM: EU keys remain under a Redwood-managed tenant with AWS KMS + Azure Key Vault dual-wrapped keys for cross-cloud parity. See attached kms-hsm-mapping_20270505.xlsx for provider and key-id mappings.
- Failover/fallthrough: we maintain cross-region immutable object snapshots and automated DNS re-pointing; in testing we saw median failover configuration time ~45 minutes. Worst-case data rehydration depends on object size but is covered by our SLA.
- Subprocessor roster highlights (from CSV): FastEdge — logs/CDN (EU); LogWatchers Ltd — monitoring (UK); SecureKeyOps — HSM key custody (DE contractor); CloudNetOps — regional cloud operator (multi-cloud). Full roster attached.

Attachments included in this message: network-dataflow-diagram_v3.pdf, kms-hsm-mapping_20270505.xlsx.

If helpful, we can run a controlled mini-migration with your security team observing and we can provide playbooks and runbooks.

Best,
Ben Carter
Head of Site Reliability
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: network-dataflow-diagram_v3.pdf, kms-hsm-mapping_20270505.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@bigenterprise.com>, security-rfp@bigenterprise.com
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwoodinference.com, ben_carter@redwoodinference.com, rachel_kim@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-06T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: RFP request — updated third-party roster + planned cloud change for EU region

Alice / BigEnterprise team — looping in a short contract note. We will include the 30-day notice for production changes in the DPA and propose the following language for the change notice clause: 

"Vendor will provide Customer with no less than thirty (30) calendar days' prior written notice of any planned change to subprocessors or cloud providers that would materially affect the geographic location, confidentiality, or processing of Customer Data. Vendor shall maintain documented rollback and recovery procedures and will make runbooks available to Customer under NDA for testing."

Rachel Kim from our security team (cc'd) will provide the cryptographic proof artifacts and key custody evidence. Stephanie/Ben — please coordinate to get the redaction-friendly artifacts to Rachel by EOD Friday so we can attach them to the DPA package.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

--
Note: this message forwards the attachments supplied earlier and references the SOC2 attestation for inclusion in the contract packet.
